newsitem.title: ITALY: Treu sees good chance of Italy metalworkers deal.
newsitem.headline: Treu sees good chance of Italy metalworkers deal.

text.p: Labour Minister Tiziano Treu said on Monday he believed a new government proposal to end a pay dispute in Italy's engineering and metalworking industry would be acceptable to both sides.
Treu spoke following all-night talks between unions, employers and the government in the protracted dispute.
"I think we did some good work last night. The government's proposal broadly incorporates the positions...so I think it should be accepted," Treu told Italian television.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi's office said earlier that the government had proposed a 30-month national contract period to replace a two-year contract which expired last June.
Under the proposal, the employers would make a one-off payment of 512,000 lire ($316) paid in two tranches during the first six months.
It would be followed by graduated monthly wage increases totalling 200,000 lire ($124) during the rest of the contract, the statement said.

The three unions, FIM, FIOM and UILM, and the employers' group Federmecannica are expected to give their response to the government proposal by Tuesday. UILM leader Luigi Angeletti said he was "optimistic" about a deal.
The dispute involves some 1.7 million workers in a sector which accounts for 40 percent of industrial output.
Any settlement is likely to set the tone for other pay accords and prove key to Italy's hopes of containing inflation.
